before.task: Compare two winter coats you own.
before.student_text: The red coat is more warm than the blue one, but it has a lighter lining. I wear it on cold mornings and keep the other coat in my bag when the weather may change. Both are useful in winter.
before.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: The red coat is warmer than the blue one, but it has a lighter lining. I wear it on cold mornings and keep the other coat in my bag when the weather may change. Both are useful in winter.

errors.explanation: Use warmer as the comparative form of warm.

after.task: Compare two winter coats you own.

before.task: Write about buying things for a new room.
before.student_text: We moved into a larger flat last month and needed some furniture. The shop sells several useful furnitures, including tables, chairs, and lamps. We chose a small desk for my room and a sofa for the living room.
before.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: We moved into a larger flat last month and needed some furniture. The shop sells several useful pieces of furniture, including tables, chairs, and lamps. We chose a small desk for my room and a sofa for the living room.

errors.explanation: Furniture is uncountable in English; use pieces of furniture when counting individual items.

before.task: Tell a friend how a neighbor helped you.
before.student_text: Last night, the heating stopped working and the room became cold. I asked my neighbor if she could borrow me a blanket, and she brought one from upstairs. I thanked her and returned it this morning before she left for work.
before.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: Last night, the heating stopped working and the room became cold. I asked my neighbor if she could lend me a blanket, and she brought one from upstairs. I thanked her and returned it this morning before she left for work.

errors.explanation: Ask the other person to lend you something; borrow describes the person who receives it.

errors.explanation: Use the base form lend after the modal verb could.

before.task: Write about something you have learned this year.
before.student_text: I have learn to make simple meals this year. First, my mother show me how to cook rice, and then I make soup by myself. I also learned to set the table for guests when they visit.
before.english_variant: British and American standard variants accepted

gold.corrected_text: I have learned to make simple meals this year. First, my mother showed me how to cook rice, and then I made soup by myself. I also learned to set the table for guests when they visit.

errors.explanation: Use the past participle learned after have.
Use showed for the completed demonstration.
Use made for the completed cooking action.

gold.corrected_text: I have learned to make simple meals this year. Last month, my mother taught me how to cook rice. Yesterday, I made soup by myself, and I also learned to set the table for guests.

errors.explanation: Use the past participle learned or learnt after have.
The past tense of teach is taught.
